newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gazprom to pay over 3 trln rbls in tax by June 20.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom to pay over 3 trln rbls in tax by June 20.

text.p: Russia's Gazprom natural gas monopoly, under pressure to pay off its tax and other arrears, is making headway in its payments backlog, Deputy Economy Minister Alexander Smirnov said on Tuesday.

He said Gazprom, the world's largest gas producer, recently paid 1.3 trillion roubles ($226 million) into the state pension fund and would pay over three trillion roubles ($522 million) to federal coffers by June 20.
"We have no doubts that Gazprom will pay," he said by telephone.
First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais said last month that Gazprom would pay all its tax debts by the end of June and had already cleared out 2.2 trillion roubles ($382 million).

First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov, who is also the fuel and energy minister and in charge of reforming Russia's natural monopolies, had previously put Gazprom's total debts to the government at 14.8 trillion roubles ($2.6 billion).
Gazprom plans to raise $2-3 billion on international financial markets within six months, part of which the company is likely to use to pay off its debts, analysts say.
Gazprom has mandated Dutch bank ABN-Amro and U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs to arrange the issues.
